note: Mixed provenance, see each metric's tier and docs/thresholds-sources.md. nasa = number stated in NASA-STD-3001; derived = computed from or taken from another NASA document; clinical = AHA/ACC reference, not NASA; engineering = our choice; provisional = placeholder, not clinical guidance.

hr.source: While exercising, heart rate is judged against the AHA vigorous-exercise zone of 70-85 % of maximum (heart.org, Target Heart Rates), with our assumed peak of 180 bpm: caution about 78 %, warning about 89 %, critical about 97 %
AHA (heart.org, Target Heart Rates): typical adult resting range 60-100 bpm; athletes can be lower. No NASA numeric limit exists. Warning and critical levels are ours

spo2.source: Caution 94 %: British Thoracic Society oxygen guideline for adults (default target 94-98 %, oxygen indicated below 94 %; 88-92 % is the target for people at risk of hypercapnic failure). Read from BTS summaries, not the full guideline. Warning 92 % and critical 88 % are ours. No NASA numeric limit and no NASA table of pO2 against SpO2; the 85 % floor of the O2-fault scenario is our assumption

bpSys.source: 2017 ACC/AHA categories as shown by AHA (heart.org, Understanding Blood Pressure Readings): normal under 120/80, stage 1 130-139 or 80-89, stage 2 140 or 90 and above, emergency above 180 or 120. No NASA numeric limit. Warning and low-side levels are ours

bpDia.source: 2017 ACC/AHA categories as shown by AHA (heart.org): stage 1 80-89, stage 2 90 and above, emergency above 120. No NASA numeric limit. Our levels are placed near these, not equal

respRate.source: NICE sepsis guideline NG51: respiratory rate 21-24/min is a medium-risk marker, 25 or more is high risk (read from NICE summaries). Low side and critical 32 are ours. No NASA numeric limit

temp.source: Low caution 36.0 C matches the NICE sepsis guideline marker (tympanic temperature below 36 C); every other level is ours. No NASA numeric limit for body temperature

co2.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2 [V2 6004]: 1-hour average at most 3 mmHg (OCHMO-TB-004 Rev D). Warning 4.5 mmHg = symptom onset in the brief; critical is our choice

humidity.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2: crew-health range 25 to 75 % RH [V2 6012] (warning); comfort zone 30 to 60 % RH [V2 6013] (caution); critical 20 / 80 % is our choice

noise.source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 2: NC-50 for work areas [V2 6078] is the warning limit. NC-40 applies only to crew sleep areas [V2 6079], so it is not used as an alarm here; caution NC-45 and critical NC-60 are our choice. Real NC needs an octave-band spectrum; this is a single simulated NC rating

airflow.source: ISS cabin design range 0.05-0.2 m/s (Perry et al., NTRS 20120015343, Table 1) used as the warning limits. This is an ISS design parameter, not a NASA-STD-3001 requirement ([V2 6107] is qualitative). Caution and critical are ours

o2.source: Derived from ppO2 at 760 mmHg total pressure, NASA Human Integration Design Handbook (SP-2010-3407 Rev 1) 6.2.2.2: caution 19.5 % = 148 mmHg (OSHA minimum, quoted there); warning 18 % = 137 mmHg (Table 6.2-4 'accepted limit of alertness'); critical 16 % = 122 mmHg (Shuttle mask donning at 121 mmHg). NASA-STD-3001 itself gives no alarm value

doseRate.source: No NASA numeric trigger ([V2 6100]); about 3x, 7x and 19x the 0.5 mSv/day background

dose.source: Anchored to the 250 mSv design-reference SPE limit [V1 4031] (OCHMO-TB-020 Rev E); critical = 250 mSv, caution and warning are 10 % and 40 % of it (ours)
